Inspect a document's history

Source: R/history.R
grist_doc_history.Rd

Grist keeps a history of the changes made to a document, and takes snapshots (backups) of it as it is edited.

  • grist_doc_history() lists the document's states, one per action in its history.

  • grist_snapshots() lists snapshots of the document.

  • grist_doc_compare() compares two states of a document and summarises what changed.

These functions only read history. To read data as it was in a snapshot, pass the snapshot's doc_id to grist_doc() with the same server, then use the usual functions, e.g. grist_doc(doc_id) |> grist_records("People").

Usage

grist_doc_history(doc)

grist_snapshots(doc, raw = FALSE)

grist_doc_compare(doc, left = NULL, right = NULL, max_rows = NULL)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

raw

If TRUE, include snapshots that are not in the snapshot inventory.

left, right

Hashes of the states to compare, as listed in the hash column of grist_doc_history(). NULL means the current state.

max_rows

Maximum number of changed rows Grist includes in the details it computes. Row counts in changes cover only those rows, so a small max_rows can undercount.

Value

grist_doc_history() returns a data frame with columns n (the action number) and hash, newest first.

grist_snapshots() returns a data frame with columns snapshot_id, last_modified (POSIXct, in UTC) and doc_id, newest first. The newest snapshot may have the ID "current".

grist_doc_compare() returns a list with:

  • summary: how the two states relate. "same"; "left" or "right" when only that side has additional actions; "both" when each side has changes the other lacks; or "unrelated".

  • left, right and parent: the compared states and their most recent common ancestor, each a list with n and hash (parent is NULL if there is none).

  • changes: a data frame with one row per side ("left" or "right", relative to the ancestor) and table, with columns rows_added, rows_updated, rows_removed, columns_changed and internal (TRUE for Grist's own _grist_* metadata tables, which change when the schema or layout changes).

See also

Other history: grist_snapshot_restore()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")

history <- grist_doc_history(doc)
history

# What changed since the first state?
comparison <- grist_doc_compare(doc, left = history$hash[nrow(history)])
comparison$summary
comparison$changes

grist_snapshots(doc)
}
